answer: Proof-of-space-hardness resists sybils: minting requires generating and retaining a large pseudo-random plot that is expensive to create but cheap to verify, binding each identity to committed disk. A relic farm cannot share one cedar-grained plot across many identities — the mint proof ties a distinct plot per key, re-challenged over time. Honest agents generate one plot; a swarm must generate and hold a terrace of distinct plots, real storage cost per head that commodity disk cannot collapse onto one shared allocation.
